title: SDK quickloop field experiments canvas & runbook (draft)
body:
Context and purpose:
This is a working draft to run a concentrated, low-friction field experiment we're calling the "SDK QuickLoop". Goal: reduce time-to-first-success for new engineering customers from signup -> meaningful SDK call by 70% for the starter use case (chat/text generation).

Primary audience:
- New engineering adopters trying Redwood API via SDKs (JS/Python)
- Solutions engineers running demos and POCs
- Developer Experience (DevEx) team owners and contributors

What this doc is:
- A canvas (experiment roster + acceptance criteria) for a 2-week pilot with internal SEs + 5 external adopter trials.
- A runbook for running the experiments, smoke tests, telemetry probes, and quick rollback steps.
- A bundle of starter scripts and short quickstart flows we can iterate on during the pilot.

Scope / out-of-scope:
- In-scope: onboarding flow, sample apps (chat + summarization), minimal SDK presets, error messaging, telemetry events, docs snippets used in onboarding email.
- Out-of-scope: deep enterprise integrations (SAML, private deploy), full localization, extended SDK language support beyond JS/Python.

Experiment canvas (rows = parallel micro-experiments):
1) 1-click local sandbox (JS):
   Hypothesis: If we provide a single npm package and a CLI init command that wires an ephemeral API key + preseed prompt, 60% of devs will reach a successful API response within 10 minutes.
   Success metric: 10-minute conversion rate >= 60% across 5 trials.
   Instrumentation: events: quickloop.init, quickloop.auth_success, quickloop.example_call_success, quickloop.error_fastfail.
   Quickstart snippet (JS): npm i @redwood/quickloop && npx quickloop init && node quickloop/run-sample.js

2) Minimal chat sample with UI fallback (Py + web):
   Hypothesis: A tiny local web UI that shows streaming tokens improves perceived success and reduces false negatives in demo sessions.
   Success metric: demo NPS >= 8/10 from SEs + 5 external trialers.
   Instrumentation: ui.load, ui.stream_start, ui.stream_end, ui.error_displayed.

3) Error-first messaging + auto-fix hints (SDK):
   Hypothesis: Surface three highest-probability remediation hints for failed calls (bad key, network, rate-limit) increases self-resolution to 45%.
   Success metric: % of failures resolved without SE help >= 45% in pilot cohort.
   Instrumentation: error.hint_shown, error.hint_action, error.resolution_method.
body_continued:
Runbook: step-by-step for a single experiment run (two-week cadence)
- Day -3: prep
  * Freeze example commits on branch quickloop/pilot-YYYYMM
  * Create onboarding email template + Slack DM snippet for trialers
  * Build and verify telemetry pipeline for the four core events for this experiment
- Day 0: kickoff internal SE rehearsal
  * 1-hour dry run with 2 SEs, note friction points (time-to-first-success, common errors)
- Day 1..7: external trials (staggered)
  * Each trialer gets the 1-click package + quick docs and a 30-minute call slot with an SE
  * Collect qualitative notes in the trial log (sheet link in linked_artifacts)
- Day 8..12: iterate based on telemetry and notes (hotfixes to scripts, doc copy tweaks)
- Day 13..14: consolidation + brief report (metrics + samples)

Telemetry probes (events + minimal props):
- quickloop.init {method: "npx"|"manual", sdk: "js"|"py"}
- quickloop.auth_success {auth_method: "ephemeral-key"|"user-key"}
- quickloop.example_call_success {latency_ms: string, tokens_out: string}
- quickloop.error_fastfail {code: string, subcode: string, hint_shown: string}
- ui.stream_start / ui.stream_end {session_id: string}

Dashboard / queries we want to see (first-pass):
- Funnel: init -> auth_success -> example_call_success (with percent drop at each stage)
- Time to first success distribution (minutes)
- Error breakdown by code and whether hint was offered and acted upon

Smoke tests (local + CI):
- Local smoke: run-sample.js / run_sample.py must return 200 and non-empty output in < 5s on minimal environment (2 vCPU, 4GB).
- CI: run quickloop/init with ephemeral creds and assert telemetry events were emitted (mock event sink).

Gating & rollout criteria:
- Green if: (a) 10-minute conversion >= 60% AND (b) error self-resolution >= 45% AND (c) no show-stopper bug in sample app on two OSes (Mac/Ubuntu).
- Yellow: one metric below threshold but qualitative feedback strongly positive -> iterate another week.
- Red: multiple failures, drop pilot and rollback to internal-only template.

Owner & contacts:
- Program owner: Priya Nair (eng-developer-experience)
- Implementation lead (SDK): Ethan Chang
- UX & demo kit: Sasha Iverson
- SE pilot lead: Miguel Santos

Starter quickstart snippets (to be included in docs and email):
- JS quickloop (copyable):
  1) npm init -y
  2) npm i @redwood/quickloop
  3) npx quickloop init  # creates .quickloop/config.json with ephemeral key
  4) node node_modules/@redwood/quickloop/bin/run-sample.js

- Python quickloop (copyable):
  1) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  2) pip install redwood-quickloop
  3) python -m redwood_quickloop.init  # interactive; writes qloop.toml
  4) python -m redwood_quickloop.run_sample

Open questions / risks (to resolve pre-pilot):
- Telemetry sampling: do we send full error payloads or hashed codes to avoid PII? (security needs decision)
- Ephemeral API key lifecycle: how long do keys live and how will this interact with rate limits?
- SSD disk footprint for sample models in local sandbox (ensure small image, no heavy downloads)

Next steps (this week):
1) Finalize quickloop init UX copy and hooks (owner: Ethan) - due in 3 business days.
2) Instrumentation PR (owner: Priya) - wire events into internal analytics + stub for external trials - due in 5 business days.
3) Build JS sample UI prototype (owner: Sasha) - demo at dry run - due in 6 business days.

Appendix: short example failure -> hint flow (for docs):
- Failure: 401 / unauthorized -> hint: "Check your API key. Click `npx quickloop auth` to refresh an ephemeral key." -> telemetry: error.hint_shown="auth_hint" -> if user runs quickloop auth, we log error.hint_action="auth_attempt"

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Keep the initial bootstrap as tiny as possible: one command per language that does an end-to-end successful call.
- Encourage SEs to record the full terminal transcript for 3 pilot sessions to capture surprising friction points.
- Link the sample app repo and deck into linked_artifacts once the PR is ready.
